en_summary: Helpful to learn supply chain dynamics even if not investing in lasers or SIVE. In shortages expanding suppliers creates opportunities. LITE sold out into 2027 causing hyperscalers to sign LTAs with capacity sold out into 2029 and approaching MTSI / AAOI + others. JBL 1.6T LRO program scaling up in H2 2027 from upstream disclosures.
ko_summary: 레이저나 SIVE에 투자하지 않더라도 공급망 역학을 배우는 것이 도움이 된다. 부족 시 공급업체 확대가 기회를 만든다. LITE가 2027년까지 매진되어 하이퍼스케일러가 LTA를 체결하고 용량이 2029년까지 매진되며 MTSI / AAOI 등에 접근한다. 상류 공시에 따르면 JBL 1.6T LRO 프로그램이 2027년 하반기에 확장된다.
text:
I think it's always helpful to learn what's going on in the supply chain, even if you're not an investor in lasers or $SIVE. 

There's a lot of dynamics + game theory that goes on in supply shortages like: 

- Expanding supplier # during shortages -> more opportunities for others.  

- or as seen with $LITE sold out into 2027 -> causes other hyperscalers to sign LTAs -> capacity sold out into 2029 -> hyperscalers approach $MTSI / $AAOI + others for their own ramps

or different opportunities from supply procurement info like $JBL 1.6T LRO program scaling up in H2 2027 from upstream disclosures.

Sivers has 100M CW DFB laser capacity online Q4 2027 during shortage with large foundry allocations. Module makers expanding suppliers, Innolight introducing new ones and signing 2-3 year contracts. COHR, LITE sold out into 2029, AAOI redirected. Higher odds of capacity agreements with SIVE. Targeting 50-60%+ gross margins. Pre-2024 focused on custom CPO, now ramping mass market 70/100/200mW lasers for 800g/1.6T. Conversion from lidar customer AEVA and ongoing AAPL.
ko_summary: 공급망 알파로 SIVE를 좋아하지만 지난 실적 후 톨 포피 신드롬이 하락에 나타남. Sivers는 2027년 Q4에 1억 CW DFB 레이저 용량이 부족 기간에 대형 파운드리 할당과 함께 온라인. 모듈 제조업체가 공급업체 확대, Innolight이 신규 도입 및 2-3년 계약 체결. text:
Yes, I like $SIVE. It's a fun company to cover, since there's a lot of supply chain alpha here. 

But the company completely Tall Poppy Syndromed itself last earnings. 

And it's clearly shown in the drawdown. 

Bit of a longer consolidated thought and some scattered bits of supply chain info: 

- Sivers has 100M CW DFB laser capacity coming online Q4 2027 during an industry shortage. 

And very large allocations from foundries online (they were doing these quals with Win Semi + 2 others back in 2023/2024), so they can actively monetize the bottleneck today. 

The other interesting reason why bottlenecks are important (aside from ASP hikes), is because qualifications convert much faster + more likely given incentives around supply scarcity.

-> As one example, module makers have expanded the amount of suppliers, eg. (lightcounting cited companies expanding to 5-7+ suppliers from 2-3). 

Innolight, for example last month responded to a question addressing tight 1.6T DFB laser supply in 2026–2027:

- Innolight was actively introducing new suppliers last month and are planning to sign 2-3 year-long contracts to lock upstream capacity

-> This is while your biggest merchant laser companies making up the world's 600m+ EML/CW laser capacity like $COHR have redirected lasers to their own programs. $LITE sold out into 2029, Landmark also locked a lot of their capacity into 2027-2029. $AAOI was an expected player, but ended up redirecting lasers into their own transceiver programs too

en_summary: Puru Saxena notes that drawdowns are normal for the S&P 500, with ~80-95% of time below prior peaks historically, and advises staying the course for long-term equity returns as volatility is the price of admission.
ko_summary: Puru Saxena가 S&P 500 드로다운이 정상적이며 역사적으로 이전 고점 아래 시간의 약 80-95%를 보낸다고 지적하고, 변동성이 입장료이므로 장기 주식 수익을 위해 코스를 유지하라고 조언함.
text:
Drawdowns are the norm. New highs are the exception.

Historically the S&P 500 has spent ~80–95% of its time below a prior peak. Since 1871, 82% of months were underwater (price basis). Since 1950, only about 7% of trading days were at record highs.

Volatility is the price of admission. You cannot earn equity-like long-term returns with bond-like volatility; there is no free lunch. The temporary discomfort of being below your high-water mark is the cost of capturing the upside over decades.

That’s why staying the course matters for investors:

• Markets trend higher over time, but the path is jagged. Recoveries eventually erase most drawdowns. 
• Selling during declines locks in losses and risks missing the rebound. 
• The bigger risk is interrupting compounding by trying to avoid normal volatility.

Being underwater is uncomfortable but expected. The investors who do best treat drawdowns as the entry fee, not a reason to exit. Stay invested and let the long-term maths work.

text:
Palo Alto Networks CEO: The Cyber Panic Is Just Getting Started

@Jason:

“There's a cyber panic. What's going on? Is this an acute issue or is this a harbinger of things to come? And is this going to happen every 10 days?”

@nikesharora:

“Jason, I think 10 days is too long. I think these things are going to happen much faster than every 10 days.

I think part of the challenge we're seeing is we've been talking about technology debt that we all have to pay sooner than later.

And what's happened is people have not paid attention to the idea that they have to go fix their stuff.

We found out about this a few days ago. We've scanned everything in our infrastructure to make sure that there were no issues. We made sure that our products had patches available for our customers who deploy them.

So there's two ways to solve this problem, right?

One, you can go in and patch the vulnerability. You can go in, find the code, patch what has been given to you by PHP, and make it work.

The other is you can actually put it in a perimeter defense product like ours, or Cloudflare has one, or other firewalls have one.

If you put the patch there, it's a virtual patch, so any attacker trying to access that vulnerability gets stopped at the perimeter because we know what they're looking for.

Guess what? The phones keep ringing every day, and the conversation always is, ‘Now how do I get out of this? Because I'm tired of getting punched in the face every morning when I wake up.’”

"I bought through all the cycles, and I have great relationships with the sellers, and they know I'm a closer. They know that my money is different than their money."

"It is basically a dozen to 15, maybe 25 different guys. Big, giant, enormous investment companies. They just trade. Starwood goes to Blackstone, Blackstone goes to Goldman. They're just flipping it to one another."

"All those guys are sidelined. They have redemption issues. They have pension funds saying, I want my money back. It's been 5 years, dude. I'm done."

"The institutions are all kind of trapped right now. And then there's this guy Grant Cardone that was going to retail investors and never went to their well."

text:
AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile are jointly lobbying the FCC to preserve existing rules as @SpaceX moves closer to launching its own independent cellular network that would compete directly with the three major U.S. carriers.

On Oct 20th, reps from all three major U.S. wireless carriers met with FCC officials to push back against proposed changes that would give satellite companies more freedom to offer cellular service.

The carriers urged the FCC to:
• Block satellite companies from using certain 5G frequencies currently used by wireless carriers.
• Keep rules requiring satellite companies to get permission from wireless carriers before using their licensed spectrum.
• Allow wireless carriers to maintain control over these agreements, including the ability to end them.
• Reconsider proposed interference limits to protect existing cellular networks.

Based on all the public communications from these carriers, and the lobbying, they are clearly worried that SpaceX's @Starlink Mobile network is going to be a major competitor to them. Starlink Mobile will become the first network operator to deploy both satellite and terrestrial spectrum.

The FCC recently announced that they are considering new rules that could make it easier for satellite companies like SpaceX to offer cellular service without relying as heavily on existing wireless carriers, so this is partly what the three big carriers are fighting against.

NHTSA announced today that they are proposing new rules aimed at removing U.S. federal regulatory barriers for autonomous vehicles without steering wheels or pedals, such as @Tesla's Cybercab.

The proposed changes include:
• Eliminating requirements for manually operated turn signal controls in vehicles without steering wheels or pedals: "NHTSA has concluded that the self-canceling and manually operated control requirements in the current standard are unnecessary for turn signal operating units that are installed on vehicles without manually operated driving controls."

• Allowing autonomous driving systems to control turn signals, hazard lights, and high/low beams without traditional driver-operated switches.

• Removing certain dashboard indicator requirements for turn signals and high beams in vehicles without manual driving controls.

• Allowing optional cyan-colored exterior lights to indicate when a vehicle is operating autonomously, with standardized requirements for their placement, brightness, and operation.

• Eliminating outdated restrictions on vertical headlight arrangements, giving automakers greater design flexibility.

• Allowing modern integrated headlights to be tested at manufacturer-specified voltages rather than requiring 12.8 volts.

NHTSA says the changes are intended to eliminate unnecessary regulatory barriers, reduce costs, and enable innovation without compromising vehicle safety.

$CRDO getting hit pretty hard today following $MXL’s plans to enter the 1.6T AEC market.

Competition isn’t anything new here. $ALAB and several others have already been making moves into the space, and given how attractive the market is, more competition was inevitable.

Credo still has an estimated 90%+ share of the AEC market and relationships with 5/6 major hyperscalers. 

$MXL isn’t expecting initial revenues until 2027, with a more meaningful ramp in 2028.

Definitely something to monitor, but I think the market is overreacting here. $CRDO is starting to look ridiculously cheap.
